hypothesis: A byte-exact, self-contained representation of a gzip member's DEFLATE syntax decisions may expose redundancy that a direct second pass over the gzip bytes misses.
scope: Three existing local gzip corpus archives only; no CIX source or third-party changes.
decoder: A standalone Python standard-library parser/serializer records gzip header and trailer verbatim, DEFLATE block types, stored data, dynamic-tree header decisions, literal/match decisions, final padding bits, then deterministically rebuilds the original member. It rejects trailing/unsupported data.
candidates: decision container compressed with zlib level 9
decision container compressed with xz preset 1
charges: Every candidate includes container magic, original length, gzip header, DEFLATE decision representation, gzip trailer, and any wrapper produced by zlib/xz. Decoder/runtime is shared format definition, not per-file metadata.
correctness: Before real inputs: tiny fixed-Huffman, dynamic-Huffman, and stored-block gzip members. For all real representations: semantic gzip inflation equality and exact original gzip-byte reconstruction. Retained physical candidates also undergo fresh-process archive-only inverse verification.
promotion: Only a complete byte-exact candidate smaller than its source is a physical positive. This is an exploratory screen; it neither modifies nor ranks CIX and makes no novelty claim.
